blindSummary: No unit-specific trans-related law, enforcement series or incident pattern is documented. As an administrative unit with a partial legislature, protective policy here depends on the national government - public-records research into the country's transgender welfare boards notes this unit's administrative structure among the drivers of the welfare-board gap.
blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation's dispatch (26 March 2026) on the transgender-rights amendment bill passed by parliament: it removes the right to self-identification affirmed by the 2014 top-court ruling, limits legal recognition to historically recognised socio-cultural groups (including local third-gender identities) and intersex people, drops recognition for self-identified trans men, trans women and non-binary people, mandates medical certification for identity documents, and in the organisation's assessment increases the risk of wrongful prosecution; protests followed the vote in the country's largest city and elsewhere.

A broadcaster's report (26 March 2026): parliament passed the amendment bill changing how transgender people are legally defined and recognised; the government says it makes welfare benefits more accessible and strengthens the 2019 law against exploitation and trafficking, while critics warn it would exclude many trans, non-binary and gender-fluid people from legal recognition; notes roughly two million transgender people in the country and the bill awaiting presidential assent; cited as the current national framework shift bearing on every unit.

A national daily (18 August 2024): a group of trans women travelling to a medical college reported that a railway protection force officer groped one of them at a metro station while 'checking her gender', with a police complaint filed and intrusive questioning reported; cited in the country-level assessment as an example of the document-and-body 'gender check' harassment trans people face at transport hubs - an incident elsewhere in the country with no direct bearing on this state/province.
blindLocalsOnly: Welfare-board status and the documentation machinery of the 2019 law and its 2026 amendment are resident-facing: this unit's administrative dependency described above bears on services and certificates for local transgender people rather than on how visitors are treated.
